title: 思维模型详解：军事战略思维 · Day 31
title_en: Mental Models Deep Dive: Military Strategic Thinking · Day 31

questions.question: 按 Boyd 的 OODA 循环，高手的主要优势在哪里？
options: 更快地跑完整圈，让对手始终依据过期的情况做决策
收集比对手更完整的情报，在观察阶段建立信息优势
把每一步决策想得更周全，以减少行动中出错的次数
严格按观察、定向、决策、行动的顺序执行，从不跳步
questions.explanation: OODA 是回路而非流程，杠杆在循环时间而非每步更准：谁更快完成整圈，谁就把对手锁死在过期数据里。多数人花力气优化决策质量，高手优化的是整圈的周期。
questions.question_en: In Boyd's OODA loop, where does the expert's main advantage lie?
options_en: Cycling through the whole loop faster, so the opponent keeps acting on outdated reality
Gathering more complete intelligence to win the Observe stage
Thinking each decision through more carefully to make fewer mistakes
Following Observe, Orient, Decide, Act strictly in order without skipping steps
questions.explanation_en: OODA is a loop, not a procedure, and the leverage is cycle time, not precision at each step: whoever completes the loop faster locks the opponent into stale data. Most people optimize decision quality; experts optimize the length of the whole cycle.

questions.question: 一个团队背着一堆技术债。按克劳塞维茨「重心」的思路，应该先还哪一块？
options: 客诉最响、bug 最多的那一块，因为它最影响用户感受
阻塞了其他许多事情的那一块，哪怕它看起来并不起眼
规模最大、最显眼的那一块，因为它消耗的资源最多
最容易修的那一块，先拿下小胜利来积累团队信心
questions.explanation: 重心是支撑系统稳定的非线性枢纽，不一定最大、最显眼。文章说按债大小排序是错的，真正的重心是阻塞了其他十件事的那一块；客诉最响、bug 最多的地方往往是症状而非重心。
questions.question_en: A team is carrying a pile of technical debt. Applying Clausewitz's center of gravity, which piece should it pay down first?
options_en: The piece with the loudest complaints and most bugs, since users feel it most
The piece that blocks many other things, even if it looks minor
The largest, most visible piece, since it consumes the most resources
The easiest piece to fix, to build team confidence with a quick win
questions.explanation_en: A center of gravity is the nonlinear hinge that holds the system together, not necessarily the biggest or most visible part. The article says sorting debt by size is wrong; the real center is whatever blocks ten other things. Loud complaints and bug counts are usually symptoms.

questions.question: 面对「战争迷雾」式的信息残缺，文章认为正确的应对是什么？
options: 尽量推迟决策，等对手先行动暴露意图后再作反应
多投入资源做调研，直到信息足够完整再做出决定
凭经验和直觉一次性下大注，用行动的速度来弥补信息上的不足
设计信息残缺时仍能执行的决策原则，用小代价行动当探针
questions.explanation: 迷雾是对抗系统的本征属性，不是能修掉的 bug。「再调研一轮」是把它当 bug；正确做法是让决策架构在迷雾中仍然稳健，并用小注下场、以真实反应替代猜测。一次性下大注恰恰是脆弱的做法。
questions.question_en: Facing 'fog of war'—information that is always incomplete—what response does the article recommend?
options_en: Delay deciding until the opponent moves first and reveals their intent
Invest in more research until the information is complete, then decide
Make one big bet on instinct and experience, using speed to make up for missing information
Design decision rules that still work with missing information, and use cheap actions as probes
questions.explanation_en: Fog is intrinsic to adversarial systems, not a fixable bug. 'One more round of research' treats it as a bug; the right move is a decision architecture that stays robust under fog, plus small bets that replace guesses with real signal. One big bet is the fragile choice.
